translation.title: Diclofenac Epolamine Cataplasm (Pap)
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in epicondylitis of the humerus (tennis elbow, etc.) and traumatic inflammation such as bruises and sprains.
translation.usage: Adults and children aged 16 and older. For epicondylitis of the humerus: apply 1 cataplasm (pap) to the affected area twice a day (morning and evening), for no more than 14 days. For bruises and sprains: apply 1 cataplasm (pap) to the affected area once a day, for no more than 3 days. Use for as short a period as possible depending on your symptoms.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine in the first or second trimester of pregnancy, if you are a pregnant woman past the fifth month of pregnancy, breastfeeding, a child under 16, if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it, if you have or have had hypersensitivity reactions or asthma caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if you have peptic ulcer, or if you are a patient undergoing coronary artery bypass graft surgery. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if it is used for inflammation accompanied by infection or for chronic conditions (degenerative arthritis (osteoarthritis), etc.), if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy, having difficulty conceiving or undergoing fertility testing, elderly, or a patient with bronchial asthma, hypertension, or edema, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol. If symptoms do not improve after use for the recommended period, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Do not apply to the eyes, mucous membranes, areas with damaged skin surface (erosion, eczema, skin inflammation, burns, wounds, etc.), or skin with lesions. Do not use with an occlusive dressing. If you have experienced drowsiness or central nervous system disturbances after using non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, refrain from driving or operating machinery (although topical products are unlikely to cause such disturbances). While using this medicine, do not apply other diclofenac products or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs topically or use them orally. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are using loop diuretics (furosemide, etc.), thiazide diuretics, drugs that interfere with blood clotting (warfarin, etc.), antiplatelet agents (aspirin, etc.), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. Itching, redness, erythema, rash, application-site reactions, or allergic dermatitis, and rarely anaphylactoid symptoms (hives, difficulty breathing, etc.) may occur. If any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, or toxic epidermal necrolysis, or serious gastrointestinal reactions including bleeding, ulcer, or perforation of the stomach or intestine occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature, keep out of reach of children, and use within 3 months after opening.
